To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the link between L1 words and their semantic representation is not statistically significant different when the word is presented either visually or in auditory format.

the reaction times of L2 learners in matching a word with its semantic representation were significantly slower when the word was presented in auditory modality compared to the visual modality, while there were no significant difference between modalities for the L1.
the L1 word to meaning connection is the same regardless of the modality of presentation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the link between a word and its semantic representations, and the role that the L2 phonological representations play in the process of activating the semantic representations of L2 words.
the relationship between the word and its meaning in the two modalities, the visual and auditory.
the link between a word and its semantic representations in the L1 and L2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the L1 word and L2 word have a similar link to their semantic representations in the visual modality.
the L1 words are activated faster than L2 words, but there is no difference between the L1 and L2 words in the activation of their semantic representations.
in the case of an L1 word, the link to its semantic representation is equally quick in the two modalities, while in an L2 word, the link is faster in the visual modality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the L2 word picture matching task is faster when the L2 word is presented in visual form rather than in auditory form.
the link between a word and its semantic is stronger in the L1 than the L2 and that the link is stronger when the word is visually presented.
the link between a word and its meaning is stronger in the L1 than the L2 and that the auditory modality is not the most effective modality for L2 words.
The main takeaway from our work is that
L2 words presented auditorily are slower in activating the semantic representation than the L2 words presented visually.
there are no significant differences in the speed of the word meaning connection when the word is presented in L1.
the link between a word and its semantic meaning is stronger when it is presented in the native language.
